name: sysctl-network-extended
description: Extended IPv4/IPv6 network-stack sysctls (CIS 3.x, IPv6 parity).  Absent keys/paths SKIP, never false-fail.

rules.title: net.ipv4.conf.all.secure_redirects (want 0)
rules.rationale: Even 'secure' ICMP redirects let a gateway reshape your routing — only accept from none.

rules.title: net.ipv4.conf.default.secure_redirects (want 0)
rules.rationale: Same as above for interfaces brought up later.

rules.title: net.ipv4.conf.default.log_martians (want 1)
rules.rationale: Log impossible source addresses on new interfaces too — early spoofing warning.

rules.title: net.ipv4.tcp_rfc1337 (want 1)
rules.rationale: RFC1337 protection drops the TIME-WAIT assassination hazard.

rules.title: net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_redirects (want 0)
rules.rationale: IPv6 redirect-reroute protection on interfaces brought up later.

rules.title: net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_source_route (want 0)
rules.rationale: Source-routed IPv6 packets can dictate their own return path — spoofing aid.

rules.title: net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_source_route (want 0)
rules.rationale: Same, for interfaces brought up later.

rules.title: net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra (want 0)
rules.rationale: A rogue router advertisement can hijack your default gateway; disable RA on non-routers.

rules.title: net.ipv4.ip_forward (want 0)
rules.rationale: IP forwarding turns a host into a router; leave it off unless it genuinely routes.
rules.fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0 (skip if this box is a router/VM host/VPN gateway).

rules.title: net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding (want 0)
rules.rationale: IPv6 forwarding equivalent — off unless this host really routes IPv6.

rules.title: net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_ignore (want 1)
rules.rationale: Restricting ARP replies reduces ARP-cache-poisoning surface on multi-homed hosts.

rules.title: net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_announce (want 1)
rules.rationale: Conservative ARP announcements avoid leaking addresses across interfaces.
